statement: An author never judges its own output.
justification: Independent reviews found defects the author missed; author self-review is void. Claude and native Codex reviews cover the required lenses in one independent context by default, split when risk warrants it, and separately verify actual findings. Native evidence revalidates completed child sessions and exact Git targets; version 2 deltas settle prior findings without repeating a full audit. Old-format records are read-only until no unexpired references remain; old registration is removed. Consecutive independently approved chains require ancestor boundaries and complete interval coverage; a boundary difference may only be a verified comment deletion. Final tests remain required. Reviewed content may be reused after mechanically verified whole ordinary-comment deletion in supported syntax, with modes, provenance, freshness and approval unchanged; uncertain syntax and behavior/tool-directive changes require review.

statement: Every done/pass claim carries machine-verifiable evidence.
justification: In the previous harness 72% of claims had no valid evidence; enforcing evidence raised real test output from 14% to 91% of claims.

statement: Changed logic ships with tests in the same diff.
justification: Test-obligation evals went from 1/1 to 3/3 only once enforced; the previous harness had no other check that a diff carries its own tests. Mechanically verified ordinary-comment deletion changes no logic and may reuse existing valid content-equivalent test evidence; test behavior changes are not exempt.

statement: Ask when ambiguous; act when clear.
why_not_stronger: Ambiguity is semantic; no deterministic trigger exists.
justification: The clarification skill triggered 6/6 on ambiguous prompts with 0/12 false fires and 4/6 on holdout prompts.

statement: Change only what the request needs, minimally, in code a person can follow; remove new and changed code comments except mandatory notices and necessary tool directives; unrelated legacy cleanup is a separate requested task.
why_not_stronger: Readability and comment exceptions need semantic judgment and source verification; regex signals are partial, and lint-checkable parts descend per repo.
justification: Implementation guidance under K5 uses a caller usage sketch, a small public surface and verified behavior slices; it reuses K3 tests and the ready-candidate review, without adding model panels or per-test approvals. The owner reported hard-to-follow AI code and repeated reliance on stale comments or comment-only fixes; K5.14 requires executable evidence and removes nonessential comments. Before requesting approval, explain the problem, concrete flow, reasons for the structure and decision order, relevant tradeoffs, verification evidence and remaining risks in the owner language, scaled to the change; the shared review policy owns this explanation contract. Keep trivial explanations to a short rationale, use one example for ordinary logic, expand high-risk boundaries, and avoid repeating an available explanation for the same candidate. The owner replaced the High-tier own-words step with a summary given before approval; the owner reads it and asks about unclear parts instead of writing 2-3 lines. Requested refactoring uses improve: discover a candidate or enter with an already specified structural change, pin current behavior before editing, verify equivalent observable behavior after each step and show a concrete reduction in reading friction. Existing staged migrations remain for external consumers; the procedure grants no delivery permission.

statement: Verification weight is proportional to risk; review a ready candidate once and use bounded deltas for fixes.
justification: The owner requested less duplicated and repeated review while preserving author-reviewer separation. Shared policy consolidates audit contexts, batches finding verification, reuses exact-target test records and uses bounded deltas in both runtimes and preserves test, evidence and approval gates. Claude callers prepare snapshots through the CLI; fallback preparation and unchanged report transport use a separate sonnet/low default, while audit and verification use opus at an effort set by the prepared risk tier: medium for smoke-only, light and standard, high for heavy or an untiered review, with an explicit caller effort winning. Findings request diagnosis rather than replacement patches; exact report checks and existing patch invalidation remain. Review/test PASS is verification evidence, not PR authorization. PR creation, including drafts, requires owner keel approve for the current candidate followed by explicit /ship1 invocation; neither condition alone suffices, and other PR requests do not bypass /ship1. Shared generated guidance and ship1 preflight state this boundary; existing hooks do not infer delivery intent from PASS. Repos whose registry row sets auto_merge=true merge on lens-review PASS plus tests without keel approve, at the owner's request for keel and keel-overlay; /ship1 and company repos keep the approval.

statement: Irreversible actions need explicit user approval.
justification: A push or merge cannot be taken back once others build on it, so a person approves it. The owner exempted repos whose registry row sets auto_merge=true, saying keel may merge once tests pass: there a lens-review PASS and tests evidence for the exact content stand in for the approval record.

statement: No secrets or private-lexicon terms in commits, PR bodies, logs or docs the agent writes; listed known values never leave the config they live in.
justification: A leaked secret or private term is public the moment it is pushed or auto-synced; rotation or history rewrite is the only remedy.

statement: No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
justification: The owner's commit and PR conventions forbid AI attribution lines.

statement: No force push to shared branches.
justification: A force push to a shared branch silently discards other people's commits.

statement: An agent never switches hooks off: no --no-verify, commit -n, core.hooksPath or hook-runner skip variables, no disableAllHooks in a settings file or a child claude, no writes to keel's settings.json or keel-fires.jsonl.
justification: keel's checks run only in hooks; a per-command skip, a settings flag or a doctored fires log removes them without a trace.

statement: Every installed Claude Code mod is reviewed: listed in the overlay's reviewed-mods.txt or committed unmodified in the overlay.
why_not_stronger: A mod runs inside Claude Code ahead of every hook, so no hook can stop it; smoke check mod-trust FAILs on an unreviewed one.
justification: A mod can approve or answer a tool call before permissions.deny and every PreToolUse hook, so one unreviewed mod voids every other floor without a trace.

statement: Every agent dispatch names a model and an effort.
Snapshot in-flight work before compaction.
A session edits only in its own worktree; live checkouts accept only exact-commit owner-approved, gate-verified fast-forwards through the guarded merge path. Ordinary live writes remain blocked.
justification: The owner requested fewer activation handoffs. A plain approval binds a committed candidate SHA; literal fast-forwards still require clean state, valid provenance, tests and exact approval. Old approvals and read acknowledgements cannot use this path.

statement: Maven builds pin the JDK version the repo requires.

After every review, explain the candidate and its rationale in the owner language before providing a concrete owner approval command or an allowed diagnostic command when no valid approval target exists.
why_not_stronger: Final-response completeness and approval-target validity require semantic context; no Codex report-gate is installed.
justification: The owner requested an explanation of why the code and logic take their chosen form before deciding approval, alongside the always-provided command; unavailable registration must not lead to invented IDs or repeated refused actions.

statement: A fix that applies a standing finding's exact replacement text verbatim and changes nothing else closes that finding without a delta review and is not reported as unresolved; recorded evidence chains still settle it in the next delta.
why_not_stronger: Whether a fix is the reviewer's text verbatim and touches nothing else needs the review finding and the diff side by side; no hook reads finding text.
justification: The owner read 'not re-reviewed' after a verbatim one-sentence fix as a request to run review again. The reviewer chose the wording, so K1 holds; paraphrased or wider fixes still take a delta, and hook gates on exact targets are unchanged.

statement: A TS/JS diff that changes three or more non-test source files runs keel precheck run after green tests and before keel review prepare, and hands its output to lens-review as an author claim the tests and contract lenses check, never as evidence.
why_not_stronger: Phase 1 first measures for two weeks whether precheck halves first-review mutation-type test findings; only then would keel review prepare warn on a missing precheck, and no deny is proposed. The runner counts first reviews of three or more non-test TS/JS source files whose reviewed tree has a keel precheck record, and lists each such review with its mutation-shaped blocking tests findings, so the two-week ratio is read from its items. Review evidence expires 14 days after it is written, so read the ratio on review_by, before the first measured reviews drop out.
justification: In 10/19-24 diffs of three or more files passed their first review 24% of the time, and chains of three or more rounds took 76% of review time; the census only ran after a second same-shape finding (O-census), so first reviews found the mutation-type gaps a machine could have listed.

statement: An Edit, Write, NotebookEdit code-cell or Bash cat or tee heredoc write adds no new or changed comments, line-start or trailing; only tool directives and legal notices pass.
justification: K5.14 comment findings were 92 of 508 merge-blocking review findings in lens-review runs 2026-10-19..28, present in 51 of 200 NEEDS_FIXES runs and the sole cause of 13, each costing a fix round and a delta review. The owner chose write-time removal over review-time detection and dropped the external-constraint exception; that reasoning goes to the reading guide. The hook compares comment lines before and after the edit, so unchanged legacy comments pass; it reads line-start and trailing comments outside string, text-block, template, heredoc and regex literals. A quote, template or text block left open on its line hides trailing comments up to the line that closes it, while line-start comments there are still denied; heredoc bodies are skipped whole. A codex apply_patch hunk is applied to the file on disk and judged in file context; a hunk that does not match the disk text line for line, or matches it at more than one place, is judged by its added lines alone, against the file and the lines it removes. It can still deny a correct line where a regex after ) or a non-keyword name holds // or /*, a raw string ends in a backslash, an f-string nests its own quote around #, a shell quote nests inside $( ) within quotes, JSX text holds //, a MySQL \' escape is followed by -- inside the same string, or a line inside a multi-line string starts with a comment marker, which the line-start rule denies as it did before trailing comments were judged. Liquibase --rollback, --comment, --preconditions and --precondition-* lines are denied, since those words also open prose. It misses a trailing comment after a quote left open (a Rust lifetime or char, a MySQL \' escape), code after the closing */ or quote of a multi-line span, and trailing // in CSS, SCSS and Less; those and the Bash writes it does not parse (echo, printf, sed -i, cp, interpreters, a redirect on a brace or subshell group or an if, while or for block, a group piped into tee) are not checked; reviews do not report comments, so the C-no-comments pass before review is what catches those gaps.

statement: A candidate that changes a code file gets the no-comments pass before keel review prepare: a fresh keel-comment-reviewer agent judges every comment in the files the diff changes against K5.14, the author deletes what it lists in a comment-only commit, reshapes each MUST KILL symbol with a test and offers each ENCODE check to the owner, and the reading guide carries its summary line.
why_not_stronger: Which comments go needs semantic judgment from a context that did not write them, and git-guard C-comments cannot see the Bash writes it does not parse or comments already in a file; no hook can tell whether a fresh reviewer ran, so the reading-guide summary line is the record until a review-prepare check is proposed from a measured miss.
justification: The owner chose a pre-review comment pass by a fresh context over review-time detection, adapted from pstack no-comments and Comment Sicko with keel K5.14 exceptions, and widened its scope to the pre-existing comments of every file a diff changes; comment-only review rounds cost a fix round and a delta review each before C-comments.
